narrative.overview:
Pharos is named after a lighthouse, and its interface works like one. The page is a cool tinted neutral, like water at dusk; the widgets are crisp white and lift off it toward a single soft beam at the top of the frame. One blue is the lamp, kept for the places where the developer's attention belongs: the current tab, the one primary action on a screen, and the prompt that says a widget needs setup. Everything else is quiet — system type, pale tonal surfaces, thin fog-colored borders. The platform team's own content and data fill the frame; Pharos itself stays in the background.

This is an Operate-mode tool, used daily and at a glance, so density stays moderate and the layout is predictable. The aim for components is soft and approachable — developers should feel the app is helping them, not auditing them, even on screens that ask for trust (capability consent, lint errors). That shows up as 6px corners, white widgets separated from the page by a single soft shadow, a low-alpha accent wash that marks the current place, and gentle 150ms transitions.

Depth here is earned by inversion plus one shadow, not by boxes stacked on boxes. The page recedes, the widgets advance, and a single ambient beam gives the frame its one moment of atmosphere. The reduced-motion policy that earlier versions left open is now settled. Appearance follows the OS by default and can be pinned to light or dark from Settings.
keyCharacteristics: One accent (Signal Blue), now with a low-alpha wash (`accent-wash`) for the current place.
Inverted surfaces: a tinted page, white widgets that lift.
Light and dark follow `prefers-color-scheme`, overridable with `data-theme` on `<html>`.
System UI type. Mono for anything a machine reads: inputs, paths, hosts, code.
One shadow family, for overlays and widget hover only. One ambient beam, app-level.
A single radius (6px) on every enclosed shape; 4px on segments nested inside one.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue appears only where it marks the current place, the next action or a needed setup step. A screen has at most one primary button.

rules.name: The Halo Rule
rules.body: The accent may appear as a low-alpha wash (`accent-wash`) or weak border (`accent-weak`) in addition to its solid fill — but only where the One Lamp Rule already allows it: the current place (active tab, selected segment), a hovered widget, focus. Never as decoration, and never a second hue.

rules.name: The Paired Theme Rule
rules.body: Each color token has a dark-mode value. System appearance follows `prefers-color-scheme`; an explicit choice is pinned with `data-theme="light|dark"` on `<html>`, which overrides the OS. A new color isn't finished until both values exist.

rules.name: The Machine Text Rule
rules.body: Text that a developer could paste into a terminal or a config file is set in mono. Prose never is.

rules.name: The Tone First, One Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth comes first from the surface inversion and a tonal step; a shadow is allowed only for overlays and widget hover, never elsewhere. If a resting surface needs separating, use tone and a Fog border, not a shadow.

rules.name: The Beam Rule
rules.body: Exactly one ambient expression of the lighthouse, at the top of the app frame. Never repeated on a widget, a card or a section.

dos: Do use the tokens (`--accent`, `--accent-wash`, `--surface`, `--border`, `--border-soft`, `--shadow-card`, `--space-*`, `--radius`) rather than literal values, and define every new color for both themes.
Do keep a single primary (Signal Blue) button per view. Make everything else a default or link button.
Do keep the page tinted and the widgets Open White, so widgets lift off the page.
Do set paths, hosts, commands, SHAs and inputs in mono (`--mono`).
Do reuse the shared widget states (empty, loading, error, needs setup) rather than designing new ones for each widget.
donts: Don't add a shadow outside the two allowed places (overlays, widget hover). Resting surfaces separate by tone and a Fog border.
Don't repeat the beam, or add a second ambient glow. It belongs once, at the top of the frame.
Don't introduce a second accent hue, or use Signal Blue — solid or washed — for decoration rather than to mark place, action or setup.
Don't load remote fonts, icon fonts or CDN assets. The strict CSP allows only the app's own scripts and styles.
Don't use browser `prompt()` or `alert()`. Use the in-app Dialog.
Don't let the platform's branding replace the Pharos frame. Platform titles appear as content.
